newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed mixed in quiet trade. October ended 40 cents firmer at $348.00 per tonne while December finished $1.10 higher at $346.20. The market was dominated by switch activity and more of that is expected ahead of the October contract's expiry on September 13.

In New York raw sugar futures ended slightly higher in thin, featureless trading. October ended 3 points higher at 12.03 cents/lb, while March closed 4 points firmer at 11.73 cents/lb. The back months ended 1 to 5 points higher. Funds continued to role out of the October contract ahead of its expiry on September 30. Total open interest in October futures remained high at 70,210 lots as of September 6.

PORTUGAL - Sugar imports in May 1996 amounted to 39,259 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 26,206 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996 (January/May) up to 126,778 tonnes against 170,208 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 amounted to 312,532 tonnes against 340,710 tonnes in 1994.

Major countries of origin in January/May 1996 were Swaziland with 27,197 tonnes raws against 15,177 tonnes, Jamaica with 18,094 tonnes compared to nil and Fiji with 16,158 tonnes compared to nil. Sugar exports in January/May 1996 amounted to 2,715 tonnes, down from 5,060 tonnes in 1995.

SWITZERLAND - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 19,912 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 18,715 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 138,516 tonnes against 124,152 tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 155,620 tonnes, up from 151,377 tonnes imported in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/July 1995/96 were Germany with 77,471 tonnes whites against 78,909 tonnes and France with 45,705 tonnes compared to 29,873 tonnes.

NEW ZEALAND - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 38,964 tonnes, sharply up from last year's 2,488 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996 (January/July) up to 151,054 tonnes, more than 50 per cent up on last year's 91,426 tonnes. Total imports in 1995 amounted to 210,379 tonnes against 215,117 tonnes in 1994.
The major country of origin in January/July 1996 was Australia with 94,225 tonnes raws against 77,384 tonnes and 51,984 tonnes whites compared to 11,920 tonnes.

Sugar exports in July 1996 amounted to 1,673 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in January/July 1996 up to 10,598 tonnes against 11,128 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 20,270 tonnes against 16,007 tonnes in 1994.
The major country of destination in January/July 1996 was New Caledonia with 2,700 tonnes whites compared to 2,833 tonnes.
